chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, who said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Mu'tab came to him and said, 'There are two men at the door.' He said, 'Let them enter.' So they entered, and one of them said, 'I am a butcher, and I sell the milk before I slaughter the sheep.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it, but link it [the milk] to the sheep of such and such a land.'

key_terms.الْمُسُوكَ: The milk (specifically from a slaughtered or to-be-slaughtered animal)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell milk before slaughtering the animal in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the pre-sale of milk (*musuk*) before slaughter, a practice that addresses the practical needs of merchants while ensuring transactional clarity. By instructing the seller to specify the lineage or geographic source of the herd, the Imam emphasizes the Shia jurisprudential principle of removing *gharar* (ambiguity) through precise identification, thereby distinguishing this specific case from general prohibitions on selling what is not yet in possession.
